write_sandbox_grimoire() {
  local ws="$1" task="$2" arm="$3" label="${4:-sprint-1}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -f "$task" ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: task yaml not found: $task"; return 2; }
  [[ "$label" =~ ^sprint-[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: invalid sprint label '$label'"; return 2; }
  local tid ttype criterion task_md
  tid="$(yq -r '.id // ""' "$task")"; ttype="$(yq -r '.type // ""' "$task")"
  criterion="$(yq -r '.criterion // ""' "$task")"
  [[ "$tid" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: task id '$tid' invalid"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$criterion" && "$criterion" != "null" ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: task $tid has no criterion"; return 2; }
  task_md="$(dirname "$task")/TASK.md"
  [[ -f "$task_md" ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: no TASK.md beside $task"; return 2; }

  local sprint_plan=true
  if [[ -n "$arm" ]]; then
    local sf="${LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml}" tg
    if tg="$(resolve_arm_toggles "$arm" "$sf" 2>/dev/null)"; then
      [[ "$(jq -r 'if has("sprint_plan") then (.sprint_plan | tostring) else "true" end' <<<"$tg")" == "false" ]] && sprint_plan=false
    fi
  fi

  local g="$ws/grimoires/loa" now
  now="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  mkdir -p "$g/context" "$g/a2a/$label"
  jq -n --arg now "$now" --arg label "$label" --arg tid "$tid" '
    {version: 1, schema_version: 1, created: $now, last_updated: $now,
     next_sprint_number: 2, global_sprint_counter: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-001",
     cycles: [{id: "cycle-001", label: ("eval task " + $tid), status: "active", created: $now,
               archived: null, archive_path: null, prd: null, sdd: null,
               sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: $label, status: "planned", created: $now, completed: null}]}],
     bugfixes: [], bugfix_cycles: []}' > "$g/ledger.json" \
    || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: ledger write failed"; return 2; }
  printf '# NOTES\n' > "$g/NOTES.md"
  {
    printf '# Task brief\n\n## Criterion\n\n%s\n\n## Task\n\n' "$criterion"
    cat "$task_md"
  } > "$g/context/task-brief.md"
  local wrote="ledger.json NOTES.md context/task-brief.md a2a/$label/"

  if [[ "$ttype" == "review-catch" && "$sprint_plan" == "true" ]]; then
    {
      printf '# Sprint Plan\n\n## Sprint %s: Review the pull request in pr/\n\n' "${label#sprint-}"
      printf 'The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.\n\n'
      printf '### Tasks\n\n- [x] Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`\n\n'
      printf '### Review scope\n\nThe gates review `pr/head.diff` (pass `--diff-file pr/head.diff` to the adversarial review). Cite findings as `head/<path>:<line>` with lines from the `pr/head/` files.\n\n'
      printf '## Success Criteria\n\n%s\n' "$criterion"
    } > "$g/sprint.md"
    local prmd="$ws/pr/PR.md" rcfx
    if [[ ! -f "$prmd" ]]; then
      rcfx="$(yq -r '.review_catch.fixture // ""' "$task")"
      case "$rcfx" in *..*|/*) rcfx="" ;; esac
      prmd="$_SM_REPO_ROOT/evals/fixtures/$rcfx/PR.md"
    fi
    [[ -f "$prmd" ]] || { _sm_err "write_sandbox_grimoire: no PR.md for review-catch task $tid"; return 2; }
    { printf '# Implementation Report: %s\n\n' "$label"; cat "$prmd"; } > "$g/a2a/$label/reviewer.md"
    wrote="$wrote sprint.md a2a/$label/reviewer.md"
  fi
  _sm_evidence grimoire "$wrote"
  return 0
}

+@test "AT-16 a7 on the whole-tree mount: every SKILL.md frontmatter stripped (body kept), every catalog default_effort medium, .checksum refreshed" {
+  extend_tree

+  run lib mount_prompt_surface "$W2" "$PT" -
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "mount=tree" ]
+  [ -f "$W2/.loa.config.yaml" ] && [ -f "$W2/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md" ] && [ -f "$W2/.claude/overrides/local.md" ]
+  run lib apply_arm_toggles "$W2" '{"effort":"medium"}' a7_effort_medium
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -qx 'effort=medium' <<<"$output"
+  grep -qx 'effort_skills_stripped=1/3' <<<"$output"
+  grep -qx 'effort_catalog=default_effort=medium in 2 entries; .checksum refreshed' <<<"$output"
+  # grep -L lists every skill: none carries a top-of-line effort: in its frontmatter
+  [ "$(cd "$W2" && grep -L '^effort:' .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "2" ]
+  awk 'NR>1 && $0=="---"{exit} /^effort:/{f=1} END{exit f}' "$W2/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  grep -qx 'effort: this body line stays' "$W2/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  grep -qx 'model: opus' "$W2/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort")) | .default_effort] | unique | join(",")' "$W2/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml")" = "medium" ]
+  [ "$(cat "$W2/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum")" = "$(sha256sum_of "$W2/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml")" ]
+  [ "$(cat "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum")" = "$(sha256sum_of "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml")" ]
+  grep -q 'default_effort: high' "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml"

+@test "AT-17 a4_no_gates: both enabled keys false at executor start and LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false in the executor env; it never leaks into another arm" {
+  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation/claude-ablation-stub.sh" STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE="$T/env"
+  run_arm a4_no_gates "$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml")" = "false" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml")" = "false" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$PT/.loa.config.yaml")" = "true" ]
+  grep -qx 'LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false' "$T/env"
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.arm_env' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.gates' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.enabled=false" ]
+  # an inherited override never reaches an arm that did not declare it
+  rm -rf "$SNAP" "$WS"; mkdir -p "$WS"
+  LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false run_arm a1_full "$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  ! grep -q '^LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=' "$T/env"
+  # the library also hands the variable to a caller-owned env file (pipeline-run.sh)
+  W2="$T/ws2"; mkdir -p "$W2"
+  ARM_ENV_FILE="$T/arm.env" run lib apply_arm_toggles "$W2" '{"gates":false}' a4_no_gates
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+@test "AT-18 a5_no_flatline leaves flatline_protocol.enabled false; a3_one_voice leaves companion_voice false in both gate blocks" {

+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml")" = "true" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.flatline' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "flatline_protocol.enabled=false" ]

+  run_arm a3_one_voice "$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml")" = "false" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice' "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml")" = "false" ]

+@test "AT-19 a1_full takes no toggles: config and kernel unchanged, evidence is only the regenerated manifest" {

+@test "AT-20 every runnable arm: the sandbox manifest is regenerated after its toggles and check-loa.sh integrity is green inside it; a tampered file then fails" {
+  extend_tree
+  S="$REPO_ROOT/$ABL_SUITE_REL"
+  for arm in a0_bare a1_full a2_no_sprint_plan a3_one_voice a4_no_gates a5_no_flatline a6_one_window a7_effort_medium; do
+    W2="$T/m-$arm"; mkdir -p "$W2"
+    tg="$(lib resolve_arm_toggles "$arm" "$S")"
+    if [[ "$(jq -r 'if has("loa_mount") then (.loa_mount | tostring) else "true" end' <<<"$tg")" != "false" ]]; then lib mount_prompt_surface "$W2" "$PT" - >/dev/null; fi
+    ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$T/ev-$arm" lib apply_arm_toggles "$W2" "$tg" "$arm"
+    ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$T/ev-$arm" lib regen_sandbox_manifest "$W2"
+    if [[ "$arm" == "a0_bare" ]]; then
+      grep -qx 'manifest_sha256=none' "$T/ev-$arm"
+      [ ! -e "$W2/.claude" ]
+      continue
+    fi
+    [ "$(grep '^manifest_sha256=' "$T/ev-$arm" | cut -d= -f2)" = "$(sha256sum_of "$W2/.claude/checksums.json")" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.algorithm' "$W2/.claude/checksums.json")" = "sha256" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.files | has(".claude/overrides/local.md") or has(".claude/checksums.json")' "$W2/.claude/checksums.json")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.files | length' "$W2/.claude/checksums.json")" = "$(cd "$W2" && find .claude -type f ! -path '.claude/overrides/*' ! -name checksums.json | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" ]
+    out="$(integrity_in "$W2")"

+    grep -qx 'FAILURES=0' <<<"$out"
+  done
+  # the manifest names the toggled bytes: a7's stripped SKILL.md hash, not the source's
+  [ "$(jq -r '.files[".claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"]' "$T/m-a7_effort_medium/.claude/checksums.json")" = "$(sha256sum_of "$T/m-a7_effort_medium/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md")" ]
+  # meta: the integrity check is live — one changed file reads Tampered
+  echo tamper >> "$T/m-a1_full/.claude/rules/zone-state.md"
+  out="$(integrity_in "$T/m-a1_full")"
+  grep -q 'Tampered: .claude/rules/zone-state.md' <<<"$out"
+  ! grep -qx 'FAILURES=0' <<<"$out"

+@test "AT-21 execute-agent in arm mode records the regenerated sandbox manifest digest" {

+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+@test "AT-22 the materialiser's fixture path rule refuses a tree holding .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/ or .run/ at its top level" {

+    run lib check_fixture_path_rule "$F"
+    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+    grep -q "holds paths the Loa mount owns: ${p%%/*}" <<<"$output"
+  done
+  F="$T/fx-clean"; mkdir -p "$F/src/.claude" "$F/tests"

+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+  [ "$(cat "$G/NOTES.md")" = "# NOTES" ]

+  ! grep -rqiE 'hidden|a[0-8]_[a-z]' "$W2/grimoires"

+  [ ! -e "$W3/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ] && [ ! -e "$W3/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md" ]

+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "beads=opt-out" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.opt_out.active' "$W5/.run/beads-state.json")" = "true" ]

+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "beads=br" ]

+}

      - name: Install Python deps for bats suites
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # Pins match cycle099-sprint-1e-tests.yml (ruamel.yaml, jsonschema),
          # the jcs-conformance suite (rfc8785), and ubuntu-latest's
          # cryptography floor. Keep pin sites in sync when rotating.
          # pyyaml: setup-python creates a CLEAN env — the suite's 16+ `import yaml`

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/freeze.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11 (PRD AC-5.1, sprint
     4	# AC-1.13, SDD §5.13, DEC-0414)
     5	#
     6	# freeze.sh writes MANIFEST.sha256 over every file under tasks/ (smoke/ with
     7	# --smoke) after validate-suite.sh passes; --check recomputes and fails on any
     8	# drift, one changed byte included, naming the path.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    13	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    14	  FZ="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/freeze.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fz.XXXXXX")"
    16	  R="$T/suite"; mkdir -p "$R"
    17	  export LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR="$T/no-prompts"
    18	  # shellcheck source=fixtures/ablation/suite-lib.bash
    19	  source "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation/suite-lib.bash"
    20	  # shellcheck source=../../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    21	  source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    22	  make_task "$R" tasks bug-fix-01 bug-fix
    23	  make_task "$R" tasks review-catch-01 review-catch
    24	}
    25	
    26	teardown() {
    27	  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
    28	  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
    29	}
    30	
    31	@test "FZ-1 freeze writes one sorted '<sha256>  <relpath>' line per file under tasks/; --check then passes" {
    32	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial
    33	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    34	  grep -q '^freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (' <<<"$output"
    35	  M="$R/MANIFEST.sha256"
    36	  [ "$(grep -c . "$M")" -eq "$(cd "$R" && find tasks -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" ]
    37	  [ "$(awk '{print $2}' "$M")" = "$(awk '{print $2}' "$M" | LC_ALL=C sort)" ]
    38	  ! grep -qv '^[0-9a-f]\{64\}  tasks/' "$M"
    39	  want="$(cd "$R" && sha256_portable tasks/bug-fix-01/task.yaml)"
    40	  grep -qxF "$want" "$M"
    41	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --check
    42	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    43	  grep -q '^freeze: OK — ' <<<"$output"
    44	}
    45	
    46	@test "FZ-2 one changed byte under tasks/ is drift: --check exits 1 and names the path; added and removed files too" {
    47	  "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial >/dev/null
    48	  f="$R/tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/tests/test_slug.py"
    49	  printf 'X' | dd of="$f" bs=1 seek=0 count=1 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
    50	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --check
    51	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    52	  grep -q 'changed  tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/tests/test_slug.py' <<<"$output"
    53	  "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial >/dev/null
    54	  echo extra > "$R/tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/tests/extra.txt"
    55	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --check
    56	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    57	  grep -q 'added    tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/tests/extra.txt' <<<"$output"
    58	  rm "$R/tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/tests/extra.txt"
    59	  "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial >/dev/null
    60	  rm "$R/tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/reference.patch"
    61	  yq -i '.reference_patch = null | .type = "refactor" | .structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_slug.py"' "$R/tasks/bug-fix-01/task.yaml"
    62	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --check
    63	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    64	  grep -q 'removed  tasks/bug-fix-01/hidden/reference.patch' <<<"$output"
    65	  grep -q 'changed  tasks/bug-fix-01/task.yaml' <<<"$output"
    66	}
    67	
    68	@test "FZ-3 an invalid suite is never frozen: exit 1, no manifest written" {
    69	  echo "uses hidden tests" >> "$R/tasks/bug-fix-01/TASK.md"
    70	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial
    71	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    72	  grep -q 'refused — the suite does not validate' <<<"$output"
    73	  [ ! -e "$R/MANIFEST.sha256" ]
    74	}
    75	
    76	@test "FZ-4 --smoke covers smoke/; without it smoke files are outside the manifest" {
    77	  make_task "$R" smoke smoke-x bug-fix
    78	  "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial >/dev/null
    79	  ! grep -q '  smoke/' "$R/MANIFEST.sha256"
    80	  "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --smoke >/dev/null
    81	  grep -q '  smoke/smoke-x/task.yaml$' "$R/MANIFEST.sha256"
    82	  echo y >> "$R/smoke/smoke-x/fixture/src/textkit/__init__.py"
    83	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --smoke --check
    84	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    85	  grep -q 'changed  smoke/smoke-x/fixture/src/textkit/__init__.py' <<<"$output"
    86	}
    87	
    88	@test "FZ-5 --check without a manifest is exit 1; usage errors are exit 2" {
    89	  run "$FZ" --root "$R" --allow-partial --check
    90	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    91	  grep -q 'no MANIFEST.sha256' <<<"$output"
    92	  run "$FZ" --bogus
    93	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    94	  run "$FZ" --root "$T/absent"
    95	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    96	}
    97	
    98	@test "FZ-6 the committed suite root's MANIFEST.sha256 matches its smoke tasks" {
    99	  run "$FZ" --smoke --allow-partial --check
   100	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   101	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# claude-stub-pipeline.sh — stand-in for the `claude` CLI in evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats.
     3	# One invocation = one pipeline phase. The phase is read from the prompt's first
     4	# line (`# Phase: <NAME>`); the stub records what the executor gave it and emits a
     5	# stream-json transcript with a system/init event (session_id), per-turn
     6	# assistant events carrying usage, and a result event.
     7	#   STUB_LOG_DIR            per call: call-<n>.argv (NUL-separated), call-<n>.env
     8	#                           (`env` output), call-<n>.fds (ls /proc/self/fd), call-<n>.phase,
     9	#                           call-<n>.pwd. The executor's `env -i` strips these
    10	#                           controls, so tests reach the stub through a wrapper that
    11	#                           records pending.env / pending.fds and then loads them.
    12	#   STUB_COST_<PHASE>       result total_cost_usd (default 0.5)
    13	#   STUB_TURNS_<PHASE>      assistant turns to emit (default 2)
    14	#   STUB_TURN_OUT_<PHASE>   output tokens per turn (default 100)
    15	#   STUB_TURN_SLEEP         seconds between turns (default 0)
    16	#   STUB_SLEEP_<PHASE>      seconds to sleep before the result event
    17	#   STUB_EXIT_<PHASE>       exit code (default 0)
    18	#   STUB_SELF_KILL_<PHASE>  1: SIGTERM itself mid-phase (a phase killed from outside)
    19	#   STUB_VERDICT_REVIEW / STUB_VERDICT_AUDIT  APPROVED (default) | CHANGES_REQUIRED
    20	#   STUB_MODEL_USED_<PHASE> model id reported in modelUsage (default: --model)
    21	#   STUB_REFUSAL_<PHASE>    1: emit a system/model_refusal_fallback event
    22	#   STUB_DOT_CLAUDE_WRITE_<PHASE>  1: emit a Write tool_use under .claude/
    23	#   STUB_LEDGER_USD_<PHASE> append a cost-ledger row of that many USD to
    24	#                           $LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH and one MODELINV row to
    25	#                           $LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH (a cheval voice call); the row's
    26	#                           calling_primitive / effort / effort_effective come from
    27	#                           STUB_PRIMITIVE_<PHASE>, STUB_HOP_EFFORT_<PHASE>,
    28	#                           STUB_HOP_EFFECTIVE_<PHASE>
    29	set -euo pipefail
    30	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" ]]; then echo "2.1.299 (Claude Code) stub"; exit 0; fi
    31	
    32	prompt="" model="" resume=""
    33	args=("$@")
    34	i=0
    35	while [[ $i -lt ${#args[@]} ]]; do
    36	  case "${args[$i]}" in
    37	    -p) prompt="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    38	    --model) model="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    39	    --resume) resume="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    40	  esac
    41	  i=$((i + 1))
    42	done
    43	phase="$(printf '%s\n' "$prompt" | sed -n '1s/^# Phase: //p')"
    44	[[ -n "$phase" ]] || phase=UNKNOWN
    45	
    46	if [[ -n "${STUB_LOG_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    47	  mkdir -p "$STUB_LOG_DIR"
    48	  n=1; while [[ -e "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.argv" ]]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    49	  printf '%s\0' "$@" > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.argv"
    50	  # the executor runs the CLI under `env -i`, so the bats wrapper (make_wrappers in
    51	  # pipeline-run.bats) captures the environment and descriptors it was given into
    52	  # pending.* BEFORE loading the stub's controls; without a wrapper, capture here
    53	  if [[ -f "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.env" ]]; then mv "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.env" "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.env"
    54	  else env | sed -E 's/^(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK)=.*/\1=<set>/' > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.env"; fi   # key name only
    55	  if [[ -f "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.fds" ]]; then mv "$STUB_LOG_DIR/pending.fds" "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.fds"
    56	  else ls "/proc/$$/fd" > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.fds" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    57	  printf '%s\n' "$phase" > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.phase"
    58	  printf '%s\n' "$PWD" > "$STUB_LOG_DIR/call-$n.pwd"
    59	fi
    60	
    61	v() { local k="$1_$phase" d="$2"; printf '%s' "${!k:-$d}"; }
    62	cost="$(v STUB_COST 0.5)"; turns="$(v STUB_TURNS 2)"; out_tok="$(v STUB_TURN_OUT 100)"
    63	used="$(v STUB_MODEL_USED "$model")"
    64	if [[ -n "$resume" ]]; then sid="$resume"; else sid="sess-$phase-$$-$RANDOM"; fi
    65	
    66	a2a="grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1"
    67	case "$phase" in
    68	  PLAN) mkdir -p grimoires/loa; printf '# Sprint plan\n\n## Success Criteria\nx\n' > grimoires/loa/sprint.md ;;
    69	  IMPLEMENT|FIX) printf '%s\n' "$phase" >> work.txt; mkdir -p "$a2a"; printf 'report %s\n' "$phase" > "$a2a/reviewer.md" ;;
    70	  BARE) printf '%s\n' "$phase" >> work.txt ;;
    71	  REVIEW|AUDIT)
    72	    if [[ "$phase" == REVIEW ]]; then vv="${STUB_VERDICT_REVIEW:-APPROVED}" f="$a2a/engineer-feedback.md" gate=review t=code_review
    73	    else vv="${STUB_VERDICT_AUDIT:-APPROVED}" f="$a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" gate=audit t=security_audit; fi
    74	    mkdir -p "$a2a"
    75	    printf 'feedback\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0}} -->\n' "$gate" "$vv" > "$f"
    76	    # the dissent envelope says what the sandbox config planned (A3 evidence)
    77	    cv="$(yq -r ".flatline_protocol.$t.companion_voice" .loa.config.yaml 2>/dev/null || echo null)"
    78	    planned=true; [[ "$cv" == false ]] && planned=false
    79	    jq -n --argjson p "$planned" '{verdict_quality: {status: "APPROVED", voices_planned: (if $p then 2 else 1 end),
    80	      voices_succeeded: (if $p then 2 else 1 end)}, metadata: {companion_voice: {planned: $p}}}' \
    81	      > "$a2a/adversarial-$gate.json"
    82	    ;;
    83	esac
    84	
    85	led="$(v STUB_LEDGER_USD 0)"
    86	if [[ "$led" != 0 && -n "${LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH:-}" ]]; then
    87	  jq -cn --argjson u "$led" '{ts: "2026-10-15T00:00:00Z", agent: "flatline-orchestrator", cost_micro_usd: ($u * 1000000 | round)}' >> "$LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH"
    88	  prim_d="adversarial-$(printf '%s' "$phase" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
    89	  prim="$(v STUB_PRIMITIVE "$prim_d")"; heff="$(v STUB_HOP_EFFORT xhigh)"; heffv="$(v STUB_HOP_EFFECTIVE "$heff")"
    90	  jq -cn --arg p "$prim" --arg e "$heff" --arg ee "$heffv" --argjson u "$led" \
    91	    '{schema_version: "1.1.0", primitive_id: "MODELINV", event_type: "model.invoke.complete", ts_utc: "2026-10-15T00:00:00.000000Z",
    92	      payload: {models_requested: ["openai:gpt-5.5"], models_succeeded: ["openai:gpt-5.5"], calling_primitive: $p,
    93	                effort: $e, effort_effective: $ee, cost_micro_usd: ($u * 1000000 | round)}}' >> "${LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH:-/dev/null}"
    94	fi
    95	printf '{"type":"system","subtype":"init","session_id":"%s","model":"%s"}\n' "$sid" "$model"
    96	if [[ "$(v STUB_REFUSAL 0)" == 1 ]]; then
    97	  printf '{"type":"system","subtype":"model_refusal_fallback","original_model":"%s","fallback_model":"other-model","api_refusal_category":"x"}\n' "$model"
    98	fi
    99	if [[ "$(v STUB_DOT_CLAUDE_WRITE 0)" == 1 ]]; then
   100	  printf '{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg-w","content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":".claude/skills/x/SKILL.md","content":"x"}}],"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1}}}\n'
   101	fi
   102	t=1
   103	while [[ $t -le $turns ]]; do
   104	  printf '{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg-%s-%d","content":[{"type":"text","text":"turn %d"}],"usage":{"input_tokens":10,"output_tokens":%d,"cache_read_input_tokens":0,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0}}}\n' \
   105	    "$phase" "$t" "$t" "$out_tok"
   106	  if [[ "$(v STUB_SELF_KILL 0)" == 1 && $t -eq 1 ]]; then kill -TERM $$; sleep 5; fi
   107	  [[ "${STUB_TURN_SLEEP:-0}" != 0 ]] && sleep "$STUB_TURN_SLEEP"
   108	  t=$((t + 1))
   109	done
   110	s="$(v STUB_SLEEP 0)"; [[ "$s" != 0 ]] && sleep "$s"
   111	printf '{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"session_id":"%s","duration_ms":1000,"num_turns":%d,"total_cost_usd":%s,"usage":{"input_tokens":%d,"output_tokens":%d,"cache_read_input_tokens":3,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4},"modelUsage":{"%s":{"inputTokens":%d,"outputTokens":%d,"costUSD":%s}}}\n' \
   112	  "$sid" "$turns" "$cost" $((turns * 10)) $((turns * out_tok)) "$used" $((turns * 10)) $((turns * out_tok)) "$cost"
   113	exit "$(v STUB_EXIT 0)"

No .claude/ # (loa_mount: false) → manifest_sha256=none, exit 0. Prints manifest_sha256=. # check_fixture_path_rule # exit 2 (offending paths on stderr) when the fixture's top level holds # .claude, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires or .run — the mount owns # those paths (DEC-0396); exit 0 otherwise. # write_sandbox_grimoire # grimoires/loa/ledger.json (one active cycle, planned, global 1; # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- resolve_arm_toggles() { local arm="$1" suite_file="${2:-}" [[ "$arm" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { _sm_err "invalid arm id '$arm'"; return 2; } local found=0 entry="" if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then # an unreadable suite file reads as "not declared" (cycle-129 behaviour: baseline still resolves to {}) entry="$(ARM="$arm" yq -o=json -I=0 '[((.arms // [])[]), ((.ab.arms // [])[])] | map(select(.id == strenv(ARM))) | .[0] // null' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)" \ || entry="" [[ -n "$entry" && "$entry" != "null" ]] && found=1 fi if [[ "$found" -eq 0 ]]; then [[ "$arm" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; } _sm_err "arm '$arm' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (arms[] / ab.arms[])" return 2 fi if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$entry")" == "true" ]]; then _sm_err "arm '$arm' is declared absent in $suite_file (never run): $(jq -r '.evidence // "no evidence"' <<<"$entry")" return 2 fi local t t="$(jq -c '.toggles // {}' <<<"$entry")" jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$t" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not an object in $suite_file"; return 2; } printf '%s' "$t" } # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to # the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed. _sm_drop_md_section() { local f="$1" heading="$2" tmpdir="$3" tmp tmp="$(mktemp "$tmpdir/.arm.XXXXXX")" awk -v h="$heading" ' $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next } skip && /^## / { skip = 0 } skip { n++; next } { print } END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n" mv "$tmp" "$f" cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n" } # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- regen_sandbox_manifest() { local ws="$1" [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; } if [[ ! -d "$ws/.claude" ]]; then _sm_evidence manifest_sha256 "none" return 0 fi local out="$ws/.claude/checksums.json" tool="${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}/tools/gen-checksums.sh" how="inline" if [[ -x "$tool" ]] && git -C "$ws" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 \ && [[ -n "$(git -C "$ws" ls-files .claude 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]]; then "$tool" --root "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $tool --root $ws failed"; return 2; } how="gen-checksums.sh" else local list="$ws/.eval/.manifest-files" sums="$ws/.eval/.manifest-sums" mkdir -p "$ws/.eval" ( cd "$ws" && find .claude -type f ! -path '.claude/overrides/*' ! -path '.claude/checksums.json' -print ) \ | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list" if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: a path under .claude/ holds a backslash"; rm -f "$list"; return 2; fi : > "$sums" local -a batch=() local f while IFS= read -r f; do batch+=("$f") if [[ ${#batch[@]} -ge 200 ]]; then ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; } batch=() fi done < "$list" if [[ ${#batch[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; } fi jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" ' {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256", files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | capture("^(?[0-9a-f]{64}) (?

.+)$") | {key: .p, value: .h}] | from_entries)}' \ < "$sums" > "$out.tmp" || { rm -f "$out.tmp" "$list" "$sums"; _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: could not write the manifest"; return 2; } mv "$out.tmp" "$out" rm -f "$list" "$sums" fi jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $out is not a manifest"; return 2; } local digest digest="$(_sm_sha256 "$out" | awk '{print $1}')" _sm_evidence manifest_files "$(jq '.files | length' "$out") ($how)" _sm_evidence manifest_sha256 "$digest" return 0 }

jq -R -n -r --argjson p "$2" --argjson budget "$3" '
    def cost(u): ((u.input_tokens // 0) * $p.in + (u.output_tokens // 0) * $p.out
                  + (u.cache_read_input_tokens // 0) * $p.cr + (u.cache_creation_input_tokens // 0) * $p.cc) / 1000000;
    reduce (inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .type == "assistant"
                                        and ((.message.usage // null) | type) == "object")) as $e
      ({order: [], u: {}, n: 0};
       .n += 1
       | ($e.message.id // ("event-" + (.n | tostring))) as $id
       | (if .u[$id] == null then .order += [$id] else . end)
       | .u[$id] = $e.message.usage)
    | [.order[] as $id | cost(.u[$id])] as $c
    | (reduce range(0; $c | length) as $i ({s: 0, x: 0};
         if .x == 0 then (.s += $c[$i]) | (if .s >= $budget then .x = ($i + 1) else . end) else . end)) as $r
    | "\($c | length) \(($c | add // 0) | round) \($r.x)"' 2>/dev/null < "$1" || echo "0 0 0"
}

IMPL_SESSION="" LAST_VERDICT="none" CUR_LABEL=""
in_container_path() { local p="$1"; printf '%s' "/workspace${p#"$WS"}"; }

# ENV_SHIM <keys-csv> <cmd…>: close every descriptor above 2 (DEC-0412), keep exactly the
# named environment variables, exec <cmd>. Used on the host (host mode, and around the
# docker client) and inside the container. No eval (eval.yml trust boundary), and secret
# values never appear in any argv: they travel in the environment only.
ENV_SHIM='import os, sys
keys = [k for k in sys.argv[1].split(",") if k]
env = {k: os.environ[k] for k in keys if k in os.environ}
os.closerange(3, 65536)
os.execvpe(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[2:], env)'
# pass-through keys, taken from the driver's environment when set; SECRET_KEYS are never
# written to an argv or a capture (recorded as <set>)
PASS_KEYS="AWS_REGION AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS_PROFILE AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL"
SECRET_KEYS=" AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK "

run_phase() {  # run_phase <name> <label>
  local name="$1" label="$2" model turns tsec prompt_file events errf argv_file
  local -a cargv envkv full
  model="$(phase_model "$name")"
  turns="$(phase_cap "$name" max_turns)"
  tsec="$(phase_timeout_s "$name")"
  prompt_file="$META/prompt-$label.md"
  events="$TRANS/events-$label.jsonl"; errf="$TRANS/stderr-$label.log"
  argv_file="$META/phase-$label.argv.json"
  build_prompt "$name" "$prompt_file"
  local why; why="$(leak_scan "$prompt_file")" || infra "phase prompt $label leaks $why"

  local resume=""
  if [[ "$SINGLE_SESSION" == true && -n "$IMPL_SESSION" ]]; then
    case "$name" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) resume="$IMPL_SESSION" ;; esac
  fi
  local cbin="$CLAUDE_BIN"; [[ "$EXECUTOR" == container ]] && cbin="${LOA_EVAL_CONTAINER_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
  cargv=("$cbin" -p "$(cat "$prompt_file")" --output-format stream-json --verbose --model "$model"
         --permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions --setting-sources project
         --tools "$TOOLS" --max-turns "$turns")
  [[ -n "$EFFORT_FLAG" ]] && cargv+=(--effort "$EFFORT_FLAG")
  [[ -n "$resume" ]] && cargv+=(--resume "$resume")

#   --claude-bin B      host-mode CLI (default $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
#   --docker-bin D      docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
#   --phase-models JSON {"PLAN": "<model id>", …} override ($LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS)
#   --phase-timeouts JSON {"IMPLEMENT": <seconds>, …} override
#   --dry-run           print the phase plan and exit 0; nothing is created
#
# Run directory layout (DEC-0413 — the grader never reads meta/):
#   sandbox/     the agent's tree (its own .git initialised at `base`)
#   snapshots/   <label>.bundle + index.json ({IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2: commit}) after
#                IMPLEMENT and each FIX
#   transcripts/ events-<label>.jsonl (stream-json), stderr-<label>.log
#   eval/        model-invoke.jsonl, cost-ledger.jsonl (copied out of
#                sandbox/.eval/ after every phase), adversarial-*.json
#   meta/        pipeline.json, phase-<label>.argv.json (argv + captured env),
#                prompt-<label>.md, arm, arm-evidence.txt, arm-env, refused.json,
#                home/ (container mode: the per-run HOME; deleted at exit)
#
# Session (D-4.3, DEC-0394 as amended, DEC-0412): `claude -p <prompt> --output-format
# stream-json --verbose --model <id> --permission-mode bypassPermissions
TASK_YAML="" ARM="" RUN_DIR="" RUN_ID="" TRIAL="" SOURCE_TREE="" SUITE_FILE=""
MAX_RUN_USD="" EXECUTOR="${LOA_EVAL_EXECUTOR:-container}" IMAGE="loa-ablation:258"
CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}" DOCKER_BIN="${EVAL_DOCKER_BIN:-docker}"
PHASE_MODELS_JSON="${LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS:-}" PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON="" DRY_RUN=false
SPRINT="sprint-1"
TOOLS_DEFAULT="Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"

die_usage() { echo "pipeline-run.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --task-yaml)      TASK_YAML="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --arm)            ARM="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --run-dir|--workspace) RUN_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --run-id)         RUN_ID="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --trial)          TRIAL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --source-tree)    SOURCE_TREE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --suite-file)     SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --max-run-usd)    MAX_RUN_USD="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --executor)       EXECUTOR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --image)          IMAGE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --claude-bin)     CLAUDE_BIN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --docker-bin)     DOCKER_BIN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase-models)   PHASE_MODELS_JSON="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase-timeouts) PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run)        DRY_RUN=true; shift ;;
    -h|--help)        sed -n '2,105p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die_usage "unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

for v in TASK_YAML ARM RUN_ID TRIAL SOURCE_TREE SUITE_FILE; do
  [[ -n "${!v}" ]] || die_usage "missing --$(echo "$v" | tr 'A-Z_' 'a-z-')"
done
[[ "$DRY_RUN" == true || -n "$RUN_DIR" ]] || die_usage "missing --run-dir"
[[ -f "$TASK_YAML" ]] || die_usage "task yaml not found: $TASK_YAML"
[[ -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || die_usage "suite file not found: $SUITE_FILE"

[[ "$TRIAL" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die_usage "--trial must be an integer"
case "$EXECUTOR" in container|host) ;; *) die_usage "--executor must be container or host" ;; esac
for t in jq yq git timeout; do command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die_usage "required tool missing: $t"; done
[[ -z "$PHASE_MODELS_JSON" ]] || jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PHASE_MODELS_JSON" || die_usage "--phase-models must be a JSON object"
[[ -z "$PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON" ]] || jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON" || die_usage "--phase-timeouts must be a JSON object"
[[ -n "$PHASE_MODELS_JSON" ]] || PHASE_MODELS_JSON='{}'
[[ -n "$PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON" ]] || PHASE_TIMEOUTS_JSON='{}'

TASK_YAML="$(cd "$(dirname "$TASK_YAML")" && pwd)/$(basename "$TASK_YAML")"
TASK_DIR="$(dirname "$TASK_YAML")"
SUITE_ROOT="$(cd "$TASK_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
SOURCE_TREE="$(cd "$SOURCE_TREE" && pwd)"

# =============================================================================
# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
#
# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
#
# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
# task_types against the known types).
#
# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
# =============================================================================
name: ablation-2.0
version: 1
source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
agy_opt_in: false
tasks:
  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
suite_version: 1
trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)

# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
phase_defaults:
  models:
    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
  # REVIEW/AUDIT 60 turns / 30 min: the Sprint 258 smoke saw a review-catch AUDIT hit 40 turns after writing its
  # verdict (DEC-0490); BARE stays the implementer-side sum (PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX)
  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 60, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 60, BARE: 170}
  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 30, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 30, BARE: 70}
  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]

arms:
  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)
  - {id: a5_no_flatline, label: A5, task_types: [build], toggles: {flatline: false},
     took_effect: [no_flatline_rows, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a6_one_window, label: A6, task_types: [build], toggles: {context_resets: false},
     took_effect: [implementer_single_session, gates_separate_sessions, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a7_effort_medium, label: A7, task_types: [all], toggles: {effort: medium},

content.text:
I found nine defects in my scope, ranked below, plus five low-severity notes. Everything listed is either reproduced in a scratch directory under /tmp or confirmed by reading the code. Nothing under /workspace/pr was modified.

**What checks out:**
- **Checksum:** sha256 of `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` is `ba767f53…122c`, which matches the `.checksum` file.
- **Bridgebuilder build manifest:** its sha256 values match `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.generated.ts` and `core/truncation.generated.ts`.
- **gpt-6.1-sol entries:** they agree across `model-config.yaml`, `generated-model-maps.sh`, the bridgebuilder `.ts`/`.js` files and `test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py`.
- **Version bump:** the `.loa-version.json` and `CLAUDE.loa.md` headers both say rc.5.

## Findings (highest severity first)

1. **`head/tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80`** — The two CI gates disagree on any path with non-ASCII characters or a `"`. This script reads `git ls-files -- .claude` without `-z`, so git C-quotes such paths (`core.quotePath`); `gen-checksums.sh:102` uses `-z` and stores the raw name. A tracked `.claude/scripts/café.md` or `a"b.md` is then reported as "untracked [other]" and the job fails (exit 1), while `gen-checksums.sh --check` passes. *Reproduced in a scratch repo.* The comment at lines 78-79 says only newlines can't be represented, which is wrong.

2. **`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:383-386`** — This breaks the trust boundary the file itself describes (lines 75 and 97-99: "no harness script sources .claude/ code"). `regen_sandbox_manifest` runs `${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE}/tools/gen-checksums.sh`, which is the prompt tree's (the PR's) copy. That script in turn sources `${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE}/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` (`gen-checksums.sh:51`). It only triggers when `<ws>` is a git repo that tracks `.claude` files. Line 513 has the same problem: it runs `bash "$ws/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh"`, which is the PR's copy. *Confirmed by reading.*

3. **`head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:64,75-76`** — Deleting files is no longer detected as tampering in submodule mounts. Once `.loa/.claude` exists, any manifest path missing from `.claude/` but present under `.loa/` is counted as "not-mounted" and never fails. So a file the mount *did* link, then deleted or unlinked, now passes with "Integrity verified" instead of `Missing:`. *Reproduced:* removing the linked `.claude/a.sh` gave `not-mounted: 1`, `FAILURES=0`.

4. **`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:20-72` (vs new steps at 175-178 and 212-224)** — The new gates won't run on most PRs they are meant to cover. The `paths:` filters were not extended: there is no `evals/**`, no `tools/gen-checksums.sh` or `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, and no `.claude/loa/**`, `.claude/rules/**`, `.claude/checksums.json` or most of `.claude/skills/**`. A PR that only edits a skill, `CLAUDE.loa.md` or the eval harness skips both the manifest gate and the eval-harness tests. *Confirmed by reading.*

5. **`head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:103-109` with `122-137` (also `144-149`)** — `run_step` calls its step inside `if ! "$@"`, and bash disables `set -e` for everything inside that call. In `overlay`, a failed `cp -P`, a failed `git add -A` or a broken `ls-files` stream is ignored. The final `git commit --allow-empty` still succeeds, so the "proof" can silently run against REF without the work-tree overlay. *Reproduced the bash behaviour:* a function with `false` mid-body under `if !` reports success.

6. **`head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:11-14,35-36` vs `133`** — `--worktree` doesn't do what the help text says when `--ref` is not HEAD. The text says it copies the work tree's *uncommitted state*. The overlay actually copies every index and untracked path from the source work tree over the REF checkout, and only deletes paths missing from the source. With `--ref` ≠ HEAD the result is REF plus the whole current work tree, not REF plus the uncommitted delta. *Confirmed by reading.*

7. **`head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:96`** — Symlinks get the wrong treatment. `[[ -f ]]` follows symlinks, so a tracked symlink to an absolute or outside-repo target is hashed by its target's contents. That hash depends on the generating machine (it breaks the "byte-identical" claim) and records the hash of a file outside the repo. Tracked dangling symlinks are skipped, but `preflight.sh:190` counts them, giving a spurious file-count mismatch. *Reproduced:* the link hashed as the outside file, the dangling link was skipped, and `ls-files` counted 7 entries against 5 in the manifest.

8. **`head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:9`** — The header says "the live manifest is only read by GC-8", but the file only has GC-1 to GC-7. Nothing checks the committed manifest here (only check-manifest-paths MP-6 does).

9. **`head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:223-227`** — The codex-headless `context_window: 400000` comment still says "the codex CLI dispatches gpt-5.5 by default". Lines 233-240 of the same change say the CLI now serves gpt-6.1-sol and no gpt-5.x name. The window value happens to match, but its stated reason is now false.

## Lower severity / worth checking

- **`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:223`** — If `evals/tests/` is missing the step only prints a WARNING. Unlike the sibling `tests/unit` step, it ignores `REQUIRE_TESTS=true`.
- **`head/evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24,30`** — The stub claims the same contract as the real library but differs from it:
  - It emits `mount=whole_tree` where the real library emits `mount=tree`, and `pipeline-run.bats:245` asserts `whole_tree`.
  - Its `resolve_arm_toggles` reads only `.arms[]` (not `.ab.arms[]`) and rejects an undeclared `baseline` instead of printing `{}`.
- **`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:131`** — Tree mode runs `cp -a` on the prompt tree's whole `.claude/`. That copies untracked local files (caches, `settings.local.json` and the like) into the agent sandbox, and keeps internal symlinks, which can dangle there. The header at line 18 says "files, never a symlink".
- **`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:326-345`** — In single-skill mounts, which don't copy `defaults/`, the effort toggle succeeds even though no `default_effort` was set (`effort_catalog=absent`). The contract text says every key gets set.
- **Unverified:** the diff changes about 15 tracked `.claude/` files but has no `.claude/checksums.json`. If that manifest is committed (MP-6 implies it is), the new `gen-checksums.sh --check` CI step and MP-6 would fail. PR.md is only 3 lines, so I couldn't tell whether the diff was trimmed.

I found 8 issues in my scope, listed below from most to least severe. I checked the validator, freeze, the cut arithmetic, the bats `!` behaviour and every arm's dry-run plan by running them on scratch copies outside `pr/` (I copied the PR files there, since `/tmp` is mounted noexec). I could not run the bats files themselves: they need repo files this PR doesn't include, such as `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/*`, `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` and `evals/fixtures/review-prs`.

1. `head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:294`, `:295`, `:313`, `:361`, `:481` and `head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38`, `:79` — these negative assertions (`! grep …`) sit in the middle of a test, so they can never fail it. Bash `set -e` ignores `!` pipelines, and a probe test with `! true` mid-test passed under the installed Bats 1.13.0. As a result these claims are never actually checked:
   - AT-14: a0_bare gets no `--append-system-prompt-file` and no `--effort`.
   - AT-15: `effort:` is stripped from the SKILL.md frontmatter.

# suite-lib.bash — fixture-suite builders for validate-suite.bats and freeze.bats
# (cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11). Sourced by the bats files; the templates are
# the two committed smoke tasks, so the fixtures follow the real schema.
#
#   make_task <root> <group> <id> <type>   copy a smoke task to <root>/<group>/<id>
#                                          as <type> (build types from smoke-build-01,
#                                          review-catch from smoke-review-01)
#   make_full_suite <root>                 four tasks of each type under tasks/

SMOKE_ROOT="${SMOKE_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke}"

make_task() {
  local root="$1" group="$2" id="$3" type="$4" src
  case "$type" in review-catch) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-review-01" ;; *) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-build-01" ;; esac
  mkdir -p "$root/$group"
  cp -a "$src" "$root/$group/$id"
  local ty="$root/$group/$id/task.yaml"
  ID="$id" TY="$type" yq -i '.id = strenv(ID) | .type = strenv(TY)' "$ty"
  if [[ "$type" != "review-catch" ]]; then
    FX="$group/$id/fixture" yq -i '.fixture = strenv(FX)' "$ty"
  fi
  if [[ "$type" == "refactor" ]]; then
    printf 'def test_structure():\n    assert True\n' > "$root/$group/$id/hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"
    yq -i '.structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"' "$ty"
  fi
}

make_full_suite() {
  local root="$1" ty i
  for ty in feature-build bug-fix refactor review-catch; do
    for i in 1 2 3 4; do make_task "$root" tasks "$ty-0$i" "$ty"; done
  done
}

content.text:
I found 9 defects: one medium-severity issue in each of `took-effect.sh` and `ablation-row.sh`, plus seven low-severity ones. I checked each by running the scripts and bats suites in a scratch copy at `/workspace/.eval/tmp/rv`, since `/tmp` is mounted noexec. All 45 tests in the three bats files pass with jq 1.7.1; with the system jq 1.6, 17 of 18 `ablation-row.bats` tests fail.

**Medium**

1. `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266` — In `integrity_clean`, the hash of `checksums.json` is only compared to the recorded `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` to add "(matches checksums.json)" to the evidence text; a mismatch still passes. An agent that edits a `.claude/` file and rewrites its entry in `checksums.json` gets `integrity_clean OK` and exit 0 (I reproduced this on a copy of a1-build). A new file added under `.claude/` also passes, because only files listed in the manifest are hashed. The tests (`took-effect.bats:195`) only cover a tampered or missing file with the manifest left alone.

2. `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:354` — In `--batch-dir` mode, `find -maxdepth 4 -name meta` also goes into each run's `sandbox/`, which the agent can write to. When I created `sandbox/meta/pipeline.json` and `sandbox/meta/arm` (naming `a8_no_ceremonies`), it was counted as a second run ("2 runs, 0 failed"), with its arm read from the sandbox. That breaks the "never from sandbox" rule (DEC-0413). An undeclared arm id written there would make the whole batch exit 2.

3. `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285` — The jq shorthand `{name, label, session_id, …}` is a compile error on jq 1.6, because `label` is a keyword there. Every row build fails under 1.6. Writing `label: .label` fixes it. `pipeline-run.sh`'s `$label` already needs jq 1.7, but `ablation-row.sh` is a host-side tool that can run on its own, and the bookworm image ships jq 1.6.

**Low**

4. `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:229` — `norm_model` strips the region prefix with `^([a-z]+\.)?anthropic\.`, which does not match `us-gov.anthropic.…` because of the hyphen. A GovCloud model id would be reported as a different model and the row marked degraded.

5. `head/evals/tests/spend.bats:83-88` — SP-6 says the default cap and reserve come from the suite's `caps` block, but the suite values (1500/250) equal the hard-coded fallbacks. It only asserts `reserve_usd == 250` and never checks the output `cap_usd`. The test would still pass if the suite file were never read.

6. Option parsing exits with 1, not the documented 2. Options parsed with `shift 2` exit 1 under `set -e` when their value is missing:
   - `head/evals/harness/spend.sh:49,55,56` (`--since`, `--cap`, `--reserve`)
   - `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:73-81` (exit 1 there means "--validate found a bad row")
   - `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:69-72`
   
   Separately, `spend.sh:62` accepts `--since 2026-13-45`, and then Python at line 119 fails with an uncaught ValueError traceback and exit 1.

7. `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:152` — The "N rows valid" count includes blank lines, which the loop skips at line 96. A file with one row and two blank lines reports "3 rows valid".

8. `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133` — `all_phases_present` also accepts the prefix case when the status is `running`. The header (lines 18-19) lists only cap_failure, agent_error and interrupted.

9. `head/evals/harness/spend.sh:150-153` — A ledger row with a `ts` but no `cost_micro_usd` is counted as a valid $0 row, not skipped as malformed. SP-4 (`spend.bats:64`) asserts that behaviour (`ledger_rows == 3`).

**Outside my scope, worth checking**

- `pipeline-run.sh:782` only takes snapshots for IMPLEMENT and FIX phases. So A0's single BARE phase leaves `snapshots` as `{}`, and every A0 row has implement/fix1/fix2 all null (`ablation-row.sh:324` only knows those three keys). A0 is the baseline in h1, so the grader may get no commit for it.
- `pipeline-run.sh:50` documents uppercase `{IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2}` keys in `index.json`, but the code writes lowercase. `ablation-row.sh` correctly uses lowercase.

**What checked out**

- **Fixtures:** `MANIFEST.json` came out byte-identical after running `regen.sh` (it holds no real checksums; `suite_manifest_sha256` is all zeros). The `pr-x` `head.diff` matches the base and head `x.sh`.
- **Spend fixtures:** the totals in SP-1 and SP-3 (15.00, 12.00, 3.00, 0.5, 14.00) are arithmetically correct.
- **Field names:** `ablation-row.sh` and `took-effect.sh` match what `pipeline-run.sh` writes, including `modelinv_lines`, `ledger_cost_usd`, `wall_ms`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256`, `refused.json`'s `.arm`/`.type`, and the lowercase snapshot keys.
- **Units:** micro-USD to USD conversions are divided by 1e6 consistently.

**Caveats**

- The PR does not include `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which `ablation-row.bats` and `took-effect.bats` copy in `setup()`. I generated it with `regen.sh`, so I couldn't confirm the committed fixtures match.
- The files under `pr/head` have lost their executable bit (the diff says 100755), so I ran `chmod +x` in the scratch copy.

head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266 — integrity_clean never fails when the sandbox's .claude/checksums.json no longer hashes to the manifest_sha256 recorded at mount time; the comparison only adds "(matches checksums.json)" to the evidence text. An agent that edits a mounted .claude/ file and rewrites its checksums.json entry (or adds a new unlisted file) passes integrity_clean. A mismatch must return 1.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:354 — `--batch-dir` uses `find -maxdepth 4 -name meta`, which also descends into each run's agent-writable sandbox/. A planted sandbox/meta/pipeline.json is counted as an extra run with an arm the agent chose, and an undeclared arm id there aborts the whole batch with exit 2. This breaks the "never read from sandbox/" boundary (DEC-0413). The search should be limited to <batch>/<run>/meta.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:383 — regen_sandbox_manifest runs `${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE}/tools/gen-checksums.sh`, which is the pinned PR tree's copy (run-arms.sh:432 sets EVAL_PROMPT_TREE to the worktree), and that script sources the PR's .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh (tools/gen-checksums.sh:51). This is PR code running on the host, which breaks the trust boundary the library documents at lines 75 and 97-99. It should use the harness's own copy or the inline hashlib path.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:512 — init_sandbox_beads runs `bash <ws>/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh` from the mounted (PR-supplied) tree with harness privileges. This is the same trust-boundary violation: no harness step may execute .claude/ code.
head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:75 — on a submodule mount (.loa/.claude present), every manifest path that is missing from .claude/ but exists under .loa/ is counted as informational "not-mounted" and never fails. Deleting or unlinking a file the mount did link now prints "Integrity verified" instead of "Missing:", so deletion stops being detected as tampering.
head/tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80 — runs `git ls-files -- .claude` without -z, so git C-quotes paths with non-ASCII characters or `"` (core.quotePath). gen-checksums.sh:102 uses -z and records the raw names, so the two new CI gates disagree: such a tracked path is reported "untracked" and the job fails. The comment at lines 78-79, which says only newlines are unrepresentable, is wrong.
head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:49 — the pull_request (and push, line 23) `paths:` filters were not extended for the new steps. evals/**, tools/gen-checksums.sh, tools/check-manifest-paths.sh, .claude/loa/** and most of .claude/skills/** are missing, so a PR touching only the eval harness, a skill or CLAUDE.loa.md skips both the new integrity-manifest gate and the new eval-harness bats step.
head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:466 — a bare `! grep …` in the middle of a test never fails it, because bash errexit ignores `!` pipelines. The "no key, token or agent socket in any argv capture" assertion (and the same pattern at 610, 652, 668-669, 682) is never enforced. Use `run ! grep …` or append `|| false`.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:294 — the new mid-test `! grep` assertions (294, 295, 313, 361, 481) are no-ops for the same reason. The checks that A0 gets no --append-system-prompt-file or --effort, that effort: is stripped, that ENFORCE never leaks into another arm, and that the grimoire carries no hidden word or arm id are all never verified.
head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38 — `! grep -qv …` mid-test (also line 79) cannot fail the test, so the manifest-line format and the smoke-exclusion assertions are never checked.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:167 — the validator's leak patterns are looser than the runtime guard. `\bD[0-9]{2}-` here (and the word-bounded arm-id match at line 171) versus `grep -E 'D[0-9]{2}-'` and `grep -F <arm id>` in pipeline-run.sh:511-515 means a suite that validates (e.g. "XD12-" or "a1_fullness") is refused at run time as infrastructure_error.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:348 — the leak scan covers TASK.md, the criterion and the prompt templates, but not the task id or test_command (both substituted into every rendered prompt) or the fixture tree (scanned by pipeline-run.sh:503-507). A task id like "hidden-fix-01" validates and then fails every phase's leak_scan.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121 — `--max-usd` rejects only the literal "0"; "0.0", "00" and "0.00" pass usd_ok, despite the "positive amount" message, and immediately cut the first trial (exit 1 with nothing launched).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:782 — snapshots are taken only after IMPLEMENT/FIX, so A0's single BARE phase leaves snapshots `{}`. Every A0 row has implement/fix1/fix2 = null (ablation-row.sh:324), and the h1 baseline arm has no graded commit, unlike every other build arm.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:708 — the jq programs use `$label` and a `label:` object key (also 224-225, 702, 816, 826, 881-882). `label` is a jq keyword before 1.7, so with jq 1.6 (Debian bookworm, the image base) every phase record fails to compile. 40 of the 52 pipeline-run.bats tests fail under jq 1.6 and all pass under 1.7.1. The jq ≥ 1.7 requirement is neither declared nor checked (pipeline-run.sh:167 only checks presence).
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285 — the shorthand `{name, label, …}` hits the same jq-1.6 keyword compile error, so every row build fails on a jq 1.6 host (17/18 ablation-row.bats tests). Write `label: .label` or require jq ≥ 1.7.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:229 — norm_model's `^([a-z]+\.)?anthropic\.` does not strip a hyphenated region prefix such as `us-gov.anthropic.…`. Such model ids are not normalised, are reported as a different model, and mark the row degraded.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:152 — "N rows valid" counts blank lines that the validation loop skips (line 96), so the reported count overstates the rows.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133 — all_phases_present also accepts a prefix of the phase set when status is `running`, which the header (lines 18-19) does not list. A SIGKILLed or still-running record passes the took-effect check.
head/evals/harness/spend.sh:150 — a ledger row without cost_micro_usd is counted as a valid USD 0 row instead of being skipped as malformed, which silently under-reports spend against the cycle cap.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:103 — run_step invokes its step inside `if ! "$@"`, which disables errexit for the whole step function. A failed cp -P, git add -A or ls-files inside `overlay` (lines 122-137) is ignored, and the final commit still succeeds, so the "proof" can run against REF without the work-tree overlay.
head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:96 — `[[ -f ]]` follows symlinks. A tracked symlink is hashed by its target's content (machine-dependent, possibly a file outside the repo), and a tracked dangling symlink is skipped while preflight.sh still counts it, producing a spurious file-count mismatch.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:19 — the `brbuild` stage builds beads_rust 0.2.6 on an unpinned `rust:1-bookworm`, but nothing copies from it, and line 82 says that version is not on crates.io and no br goes in the image. The legacy builder would fail the image on this dead stage. The "Digest pinned … node:20.11.0" comment (17-18) now sits above the wrong FROM.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85 — the header says the image ships "codex 0.137.0 by Dockerfile.ablation", but Dockerfile.ablation:25 pins CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1, so the recorded toolchain provenance is wrong.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:50 — documents snapshots/index.json keys as IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2, but line 788 writes lowercased keys (implement, fix1, fix2), which is what ablation-row.sh reads.
head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:223 — the codex-headless context_window comment still says the codex CLI dispatches gpt-5.5 by default, contradicting lines 233-240 of the same change (the CLI now serves gpt-6.1-sol).
head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:9 — the header says the live manifest is read by GC-8, but the file defines only GC-1…GC-7. Nothing in this file checks the committed manifest.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:49 — the pull_request (and push, line 23) `paths:` filters were not extended for the new steps. evals/**, tools/gen-checksums.sh, tools/check-manifest-paths.sh, .claude/loa/** and most of .claude/skills/** are missing, so a PR touching only the eval harness, a skill or CLAUDE.loa.md skips both the new integrity-manifest gate and the new eval-harness bats step.
head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:466 — a bare `! grep …` in the middle of a test never fails it, because bash errexit ignores `!` pipelines. The "no key, token or agent socket in any argv capture" assertion (and the same pattern at 610, 652, 668-669, 682) is never enforced. Use `run ! grep …` or append `|| false`.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:294 — the new mid-test `! grep` assertions (294, 295, 313, 361, 481) are no-ops for the same reason. The checks that A0 gets no --append-system-prompt-file or --effort, that effort: is stripped, that ENFORCE never leaks into another arm, and that the grimoire carries no hidden word or arm id are all never verified.
head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38 — `! grep -qv …` mid-test (also line 79) cannot fail the test, so the manifest-line format and the smoke-exclusion assertions are never checked.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:167 — the validator's leak patterns are looser than the runtime guard. `\bD[0-9]{2}-` here (and the word-bounded arm-id match at line 171) versus `grep -E 'D[0-9]{2}-'` and `grep -F <arm id>` in pipeline-run.sh:511-515 means a suite that validates (e.g. "XD12-" or "a1_fullness") is refused at run time as infrastructure_error.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:348 — the leak scan covers TASK.md, the criterion and the prompt templates, but not the task id or test_command (both substituted into every rendered prompt) or the fixture tree (scanned by pipeline-run.sh:503-507). A task id like "hidden-fix-01" validates and then fails every phase's leak_scan.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121 — `--max-usd` rejects only the literal "0"; "0.0", "00" and "0.00" pass usd_ok, despite the "positive amount" message, and immediately cut the first trial (exit 1 with nothing launched).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:782 — snapshots are taken only after IMPLEMENT/FIX, so A0's single BARE phase leaves snapshots `{}`. Every A0 row has implement/fix1/fix2 = null (ablation-row.sh:324), and the h1 baseline arm has no graded commit, unlike every other build arm.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:708 — the jq programs use `$label` and a `label:` object key (also 224-225, 702, 816, 826, 881-882). `label` is a jq keyword before 1.7, so with jq 1.6 (Debian bookworm, the image base) every phase record fails to compile. 40 of the 52 pipeline-run.bats tests fail under jq 1.6 and all pass under 1.7.1. The jq ≥ 1.7 requirement is neither declared nor checked (pipeline-run.sh:167 only checks presence).
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285 — the shorthand `{name, label, …}` hits the same jq-1.6 keyword compile error, so every row build fails on a jq 1.6 host (17/18 ablation-row.bats tests). Write `label: .label` or require jq ≥ 1.7.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:229 — norm_model's `^([a-z]+\.)?anthropic\.` does not strip a hyphenated region prefix such as `us-gov.anthropic.…`. Such model ids are not normalised, are reported as a different model, and mark the row degraded.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:152 — "N rows valid" counts blank lines that the validation loop skips (line 96), so the reported count overstates the rows.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133 — all_phases_present also accepts a prefix of the phase set when status is `running`, which the header (lines 18-19) does not list. A SIGKILLed or still-running record passes the took-effect check.
head/evals/harness/spend.sh:150 — a ledger row without cost_micro_usd is counted as a valid USD 0 row instead of being skipped as malformed, which silently under-reports spend against the cycle cap.
head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:103 — run_step invokes its step inside `if ! "$@"`, which disables errexit for the whole step function. A failed cp -P, git add -A or ls-files inside `overlay` (lines 122-137) is ignored, and the final commit still succeeds, so the "proof" can run against REF without the work-tree overlay.
head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:96 — `[[ -f ]]` follows symlinks. A tracked symlink is hashed by its target's content (machine-dependent, possibly a file outside the repo), and a tracked dangling symlink is skipped while preflight.sh still counts it, producing a spurious file-count mismatch.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:19 — the `brbuild` stage builds beads_rust 0.2.6 on an unpinned `rust:1-bookworm`, but nothing copies from it, and line 82 says that version is not on crates.io and no br goes in the image. The legacy builder would fail the image on this dead stage. The "Digest pinned … node:20.11.0" comment (17-18) now sits above the wrong FROM.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85 — the header says the image ships "codex 0.137.0 by Dockerfile.ablation", but Dockerfile.ablation:25 pins CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1, so the recorded toolchain provenance is wrong.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:50 — documents snapshots/index.json keys as IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2, but line 788 writes lowercased keys (implement, fix1, fix2), which is what ablation-row.sh reads.
head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:223 — the codex-headless context_window comment still says the codex CLI dispatches gpt-5.5 by default, contradicting lines 233-240 of the same change (the CLI now serves gpt-6.1-sol).
head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:9 — the header says the live manifest is read by GC-8, but the file defines only GC-1…GC-7. Nothing in this file checks the committed manifest.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
I wrote the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 27 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**What blocks the merge:**
- **Tamper check can be bypassed.** `took-effect.sh:266` compares `checksums.json` against the hash recorded at mount time, but a mismatch only changes the evidence text. An agent can edit a mounted `.claude/` file, update its checksum entry, and still pass `integrity_clean`.
- **Batch mode reads from the agent's sandbox.** `took-effect.sh:354` searches four levels deep for `meta` folders, so it also picks up `sandbox/meta/`, which the agent can write to. A planted run record gets counted, and an unknown arm id there aborts the whole batch.
- **PR code runs on the host.** `sandbox-mount.sh:383` runs the PR's own `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, which loads the PR's `compat-lib.sh`. Line 512 runs the PR's `update-beads-state.sh`. Both break the library's own rule that the harness never runs `.claude/` code.
- **Deleted files no longer fail the check.** In `check-loa.sh:75`, on a submodule mount, a file deleted from `.claude/` but still present under `.loa/` counts as "not-mounted" and passes.
- **The two new CI gates disagree on some file names.** `check-manifest-paths.sh:80` lists tracked files in a way that escapes names containing non-ASCII characters or quotes, while `gen-checksums.sh` records them raw. A repo with such a name fails one gate and passes the other.
- **The new CI steps mostly won't run.** The workflow's path filters (`bats-tests.yml:23`/`:49`) weren't extended, so PRs touching only `evals/**`, the new tools, or most skills skip both the manifest gate and the eval-harness tests.
- **Several key test assertions can't fail.** A `! grep` in the middle of a bats test never fails it. This disables the secret-leak, arm-id-leak, effort-stripping and manifest-format checks in `pipeline-run.bats`, `arm-toggles.bats` and `freeze.bats`.

**Lower severity (also listed in the review):**
- **Arm A0 is never snapshotted.** Only IMPLEMENT and FIX phases are snapshotted, so the baseline arm's single BARE phase has no commit to grade (`pipeline-run.sh:782`).
- **jq 1.7 or newer is required but never checked.** `pipeline-run.sh` and `ablation-row.sh` use `label` as a name, which jq 1.6 (the Debian bookworm version) rejects.
- **Smaller defects:** the suite validator is looser than the runtime leak guard, `--max-usd 0.0` gets past the check, `fresh-mount-proof.sh` ignores failed steps, and `gen-checksums.sh` follows symlinks.
- **Stale or wrong comments and docs:** the codex version, the snapshot key casing, a model-config comment, and a GC-8 test the header mentions but that doesn't exist.

**Testing:** the frozen files had lost their executable bit, so I ran the suites on a scratch copy with it restored. `pipeline-run.bats` passes all 52 tests with jq 1.7.1, and 40 fail under jq 1.6. Most other suites need repo files this PR doesn't include, so I couldn't run them as committed.

I checked the most serious findings against the code myself; the rest come from three helper reviews, which reproduced most of them in scratch copies.
